findings.claim: Unit is titled 'Physics Paper 2', implying a second physics paper.
findings.truth: J260 has ONE physics paper. Foundation Papers 1-4 are Biology /01, Chemistry /02, Physics /03 (all 95 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 26.4% each) and Combined Science /04 (75 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 20.8%); Higher mirrors as Papers 5-8. Physics /03 assesses P1-P6 plus BCP7 and BCP8. Established mapping for this unit: L1 = P4.1, L2 = P4.2, L3 = P4.3, L4 = P4.4, L5 = P5.1, L6 = P5.2, L7 = P6.1 + P6.2, L8 = P6.3 + P6.1 density. The 'physics-paper-1/2' split is Gateway-shaped and matches no OCR B paper. No lesson text asserts a paper structure, so nothing needed correcting in the content; the unit naming is Tom's call.
findings.evidence: spec assessment overview: 'Paper 3 assesses content P1 - P6 and BCP7 and 8'; J260/03 95 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 26.4%; J260/04 75 marks, 20.8%

findings.claim: L5 and L6 re-teach alpha, beta and gamma properties and background radiation.
findings.truth: The sibling unit science-ocr-b/physics-paper-1 L1 'Radiation: Risks and Benefits' already teaches ionising versus non-ionising radiation, alpha/beta/gamma and background radiation (P1.2, overlapping P5.1.7 and P5.2.1). The overlap is duplication, not an error, and nothing here is contradicted. Option A: leave both (spiral revision). Option B: trim the sibling L1 to P1.2 radiation risk only. No rename requested or made.
findings.evidence: sibling raw/L01.txt content_html; spec P1.2, P5.1.7, P5.2.1

findings.claim: Several P4-P6 assessable outcomes are taught nowhere in this unit.
findings.truth: Not taught anywhere in L1-L8: P4.3.8 inertial mass (Higher); P4.4.8 and P4.4.9 power as the rate of energy transfer, power = energy transferred / time (both tier, on the recall list) - may sit in the sibling unit's P2/P3 lessons; P5.1.2 how the atomic model changed (Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr) and P5.1.3 order of magnitude of atoms (about 10^-10 m); neutron emission, required by P5.1.7, P5.1.8 and P5.1.9 (L5 teaches 'three main types' only); P6.2.4 the link between the temperature of a gas and its pressure at constant volume (qualitative); P6.3.4 non-linear force-extension systems such as rubber bands; P6.3.6a work done stretching a spring as the area under a force-extension graph and P6.3.7 energy stored = 1/2 x spring constant x (extension)^2 (both tier, on the select-and-apply list). Each gap needs new prose and new narration, so it is a build decision, not a surgical fix.

findings.claim: A 'higher-only' wrapper hides the paragraph 'After one half-life, half the original unstable nuclei remain... 800 -> 400 -> 200 -> 100 Bq'.
findings.truth: That paragraph is the plain meaning of half-life plus repeated halving, which the spec assesses at both tiers. Only P5.1.11 (net decline expressed as a ratio after a given integral number of half-lives) is bold. Foundation students must not have the definition of half-life hidden from them. Wrapper removed; div open/close counts unchanged.
findings.evidence: bold spec P5.1.10 and P5.1.12 not bold; P5.1.11 bold

findings.claim: A 'higher-only' wrapper sits round the paragraph on the area under a velocity-time graph.
findings.truth: This wrapper is correct and was kept: P4.2.10 'Interpret enclosed areas in velocity-time graphs' is bold in the spec, so Higher tier only. The matching flashcard already carries '(Higher tier)' at the end of the question.
findings.evidence: bold spec P4.2.10

findings.claim: The momentum section is wrapped 'higher-only', but the momentum practice question, two momentum flashcards and the momentum takeaway carry no tier tag.
findings.truth: The wrapper itself is right (P4.3.4 momentum = mass x velocity, its conservation, and P4.3.5 change in momentum = resultant force x time are all bold). The untagged items test the same bold outcome, so they now carry '(Higher tier)': prefix on the practice question, end-of-question tag on flashcards 5 and 6, and an inline tag on the momentum half of the takeaway (no wrapper inside the list).
findings.evidence: bold spec P4.3.4, P4.3.5; equation list 5h shows momentum bold under 'recall and apply' and change in momentum bold under 'select and apply'

findings.claim: 'When forces act at an angle to each other, you use a scale drawing ... to find the resultant. Resolving forces into components is a Higher-tier skill'.
findings.truth: The Higher-only outcome is P4.3.3, 'use scale drawings of vector diagrams to illustrate the resolution of two or more forces', limited to parallel and perpendicular vectors. So the scale-drawing method itself is the Higher-tier skill, not only 'resolving into components'. Sentence reworded to name the right skill and its limit.
findings.evidence: bold spec P4.3.3 (bold, 'Limited to parallel and perpendicular vectors only')

findings.claim: Mark scheme for the collision question: 'some kinetic energy (and therefore momentum of the system) is transferred to the surroundings as sound, heat and deformation of materials'.
findings.truth: Momentum is conserved in a closed system; kinetic energy is not. Losing energy to sound, heating and deformation does not reduce momentum. The lesson's own body text says 'Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not', so the mark scheme contradicted the lesson. The real reason the measured velocity is lower is that friction from the road acts during the impact, so the system is not perfectly closed. Arithmetic checked and unchanged: 1400 x 15 = 21 000 kg m/s; 21 000 / 2 400 = 8.75 m/s.
findings.evidence: spec P4.3.4 'describe examples of the conservation of momentum in collisions'; recomputation 21000/2400 = 8.75

findings.claim: Flashcard question reads 'What does Name four energy stores state?'.
findings.truth: A mangled template string. Replaced with 'Name four of the energy stores that physicists use to describe a system.' The answer is unchanged and still lists eight stores to pick from.
findings.evidence: raw file flashcard_questions[6]

findings.claim: Flashcard asks for the difference between specific latent heat of fusion and of vaporisation, but the answer only defines fusion.
findings.truth: The answer now defines both: fusion is the energy per kilogram to melt or freeze; vaporisation is the energy per kilogram to boil or condense. 23 words, no comma list, no clash with any other answer in the lesson.
findings.evidence: spec P6.1.6 and the P6.1 narrative on specific latent heat

findings.claim: 'On Earth's surface, g = 10 N/kg (or 9.8 N/kg to 2 significant figures)' - in the hover definition, the body text and a flashcard answer.
findings.truth: The parenthetical is nonsense: 9.8 to two significant figures is 9.8, and 10 is the rounded value, not the precise one. The spec's own narrative fixes the teaching value: 'Near the Earth's surface, the weight of a 1 kg object is roughly 10 N. The Earth's gravitational field strength is therefore 10 N/kg.' All three now read 'g = 10 N/kg; the more precise value is 9.8 N/kg.'
findings.evidence: spec P4.1 teaching narrative ('The Earth's gravitational field strength is therefore 10 N/kg')

findings.claim: 'What are the two conditions for a Newton's Third Law force pair?' with an answer giving four conditions.
findings.truth: A Third Law pair is equal in size, opposite in direction, the same type of force, and acts on different objects - four conditions, and the lesson states all four. Question changed to ask for four.
findings.evidence: spec P4.1.1 and the P4.1 narrative ('the same kind of force, equal in size and opposite in direction, and act on different objects')

findings.claim: Match check offers 'Contact force - requires physical touching' and 'Contact force - surface push on an object' for Friction and Normal contact force.
findings.truth: Option 0 describes the normal contact force just as well as friction, so two options were effectively synonymous and the item had no single right pairing. Option 0 now says friction opposes sliding between two surfaces; option 2 now names a surface pushing on a resting object.
findings.evidence: spec P4.1.2 and P4.1.3 (friction as the interaction between sliding surfaces; normal contact force)

findings.claim: 'The engine produces a forward force of 500 N' for a cyclist and bicycle, and the mark scheme calls the resulting steady speed 'terminal velocity'.
findings.truth: A bicycle has no engine; the forward force comes from pedalling. Terminal velocity describes a falling object, not a cyclist on a flat road - the right term is a constant top speed. The arithmetic is right and unchanged: 500 - 200 = 300 N; 300 / 85 = 3.5 m/s^2.
findings.evidence: recomputation 300/85 = 3.53; spec P4.3.9

findings.claim: 'A wind turbine generates 500 000 J of electrical energy from 750 000 J of wind energy' (67%), with a mark scheme aside reading 'note: 67% is an exam-context figure, not a real-world claim'.
findings.truth: No wind turbine can reach 67%: the Betz limit caps the fraction of the wind's kinetic energy any turbine can extract at about 59%. The figures are now 500 000 J from 1 250 000 J = 40%, which sits inside the real 35-50% range the mark scheme itself quotes, and the author's aside is gone.
findings.evidence: settled fact: Betz limit = 16/27, about 59.3%; recomputation 500000/1250000 = 0.4

findings.claim: 'Explain two precautions...' marked as 3 marks, with a mark scheme reading 'Any two of: ... Maximum 3 marks'.
findings.truth: The question and its mark scheme contradicted each other. The question now asks for three precautions, each with a scientific reason, for 1 mark each.
findings.evidence: raw file practice_questions[5]

findings.claim: 'Use the StudyVault Mastering rubric: state the science, apply it to the context, and evaluate the consequence.'
findings.truth: A drafting aside: students never see a rubric by that name. Reworded to give the same three-step structure without the internal reference.
findings.evidence: raw file exam_tip_html

findings.claim: 'The model treats particles as identical, hard, spherical objects with no size or internal structure.'
findings.truth: Self-contradictory: hard spheres have a size. The particle model's simplification is that particles have no internal structure. 'size or' removed.
findings.evidence: spec P6.2 particle model narrative

findings.claim: The lesson teaches PET scanning and positron (beta-plus) emission.
findings.truth: The physics is right (positrons annihilate with electrons, giving pairs of gamma rays) but J260 lists only alpha, beta, neutron and gamma radiation, and P5.2.3 asks only for uses of nuclear radiations to explore internal organs and destroy unwanted tissue. This is enrichment beyond the spec, not an error, so it is left alone.

findings.claim: The hover definition and glossary entry for 'velocity-time graph' say the area under the line gives the distance travelled, with no Higher-tier flag, while the body paragraph teaching it is correctly wrapped.
findings.truth: P4.2.10 is bold, so interpreting enclosed areas is Higher tier only. Glossary and hover definitions are reference text rather than assessed teaching, and tagging them would clutter every definition, so no edit was made.
findings.evidence: bold spec P4.2.10

summary: 8 lessons checked against OCR Twenty First Century Combined Science B J260 (chapters P4 Explaining motion, P5 Radioactive materials, P6 Matter). 26 findings: 1 HIGH (a mark scheme saying momentum is lost as sound and heat, contradicting the lesson's own text), 16 MEDIUM, 9 LOW; 20 are FIX (29 edits), 3 ADJUDICATE, 3 NOTE. Every worked example, mark scheme calculation and knowledge check answer key was recomputed and all were arithmetically right; g = 10 N/kg is confirmed from the spec's P4.1 narrative. The two systematic faults are a corrupted final 'match' knowledge check in six of the eight lessons (left column made of truncated question stems) and tier drift: one wrapper hid both-tier half-life content from Foundation students, while Higher-only momentum work sat untagged outside its wrapper. No lesson makes a paper-structure claim, and no Gateway wording, AQA or Edexcel wording, banned rubric phrase, raw LaTeX in a plain-text field or corrupted '$$' was found.
